question: Should the canonical WhatsApp phone-code implementation use this plugin-owned interactive login contract, and should it preserve the existing linked-device identity rather than globally renaming every session to `Google Chrome (openclaw)`?
rationale: The plugin-local contract matches repository ownership better than the competing generic CLI expansion, but the global device-label change is not proven necessary by pinned Baileys source and affects existing paths, so maintainer intent is required before merge.

options.title: Plugin-local and identity-preserving
options.body: Keep this PR's plugin-owned login choice, remove the global browser-label change unless live evidence proves it necessary, and require exact-head device proof.

options.title: Plugin-local with global Chrome identity
options.body: Keep this PR's API shape and intentionally adopt `Google Chrome (openclaw)` for every WhatsApp path with explicit upgrade proof.

options.title: Use the generic CLI contract
options.body: Prefer the competing PR's `--phone-number` channel-auth surface and close or supersede this branch after selecting it as canonical.

recommendation.title: Plugin-local and identity-preserving
recommendation.body: Keep this PR's plugin-owned login choice, remove the global browser-label change unless live evidence proves it necessary, and require exact-head device proof.

likelyOwner.reason: Recent history shows the strongest ownership of the WhatsApp auth, identity, and runtime boundaries affected by this product and compatibility choice.
